own.claim: A data room request is a gate: it separates investors who are serious from those who are polite. Sending it the same day or next morning signals momentum and professionalism; waiting signals either disorganization or lack of interest.
own.why: Investors see this as a test of the founder's operational readiness and speed. A slow reply to a diligence request is read as a proxy for how the founder will move through the rest of the process.

own.claim: When an investor sends a term-sheet FAQ and a portfolio note alongside a diligence request, they are signaling they have already decided to move forward if the diligence is clean; the data room request is not exploratory but confirmatory.
own.why: The FAQ and portfolio note are not sent to every inquiry; they are sent to investors the firm is preparing to move with. This is a warm signal, not a cold one.

own.claim: A founder who has multiple investors in a seed wave should not treat each one as equally urgent; the one who asks for a data room first is the one most likely to move fastest and should be prioritized.
own.why: Momentum in a raise comes from one investor moving; others follow. The first to ask for diligence is the first to close, and closing one investor often triggers others to decide.

scenarios.act: If the founder replies today or tomorrow with the data room link and cap table, the investor will move to the next stage: scheduling a call or meeting to discuss the diligence material, or moving directly to a partner meeting if the material is clean. A prompt reply signals momentum and operational readiness. The investor will likely ask follow-up questions or request references or customer calls within a few days. The conversation will move toward a decision within the playbook's typical timeline for diligence (21 days).
scenarios.best: The founder sends the data room link and cap table today, with a brief note thanking the investor for the interest and offering to walk through the material on a call. The investor reviews the material over the next few days, finds it clean, and schedules a partner meeting or a call with a decision-maker. The conversation moves to diligence or a term sheet within two weeks. Banyan becomes the lead investor or a co-investor in the round, and other investors in the wave see the momentum and move faster.
scenarios.do_nothing: If the founder does not reply, the investor will interpret silence as lost momentum or lack of interest. After three to five business days of no reply, the investor will likely move on to other companies in the wave. The conversation will decay into a soft no that is never explicitly stated. The founder will learn of the pass only when the round has moved on without Banyan's participation. The investor will not follow up a second time after a diligence request goes unanswered.
